question: A developer wraps a get_temperature function in an in-process MCP server named "weather" using create_sdk_mcp_server, then passes it via mcp_servers to query(). They want the tool to run without a permission prompt, but calls to it are being denied by the default permission flow. What is most likely missing from their ClaudeAgentOptions?
options: A) disallowed_tools=[], since an empty deny list is required to clear any tool that was previously denied in some earlier, unrelated session.
B) allowed_tools=["mcp__weather__get_temperature"], since MCP tools use the name mcp__{server}__{tool} and need that full name listed to auto-approve.
C) permission_mode="bypassPermissions", since custom MCP tools can only run automatically once permission checks are bypassed for the whole session entirely.
D) allowed_tools=["get_temperature"], since auto-approval rules match against a tool's bare function name regardless of which server registered it.
correct_answers: B) allowed_tools=["mcp__weather__get_temperature"], since MCP tools use the name mcp__{server}__{tool} and need that full name listed to auto-approve.
explanations: disallowed_tools controls deny rules and an empty array has no special effect on unblocking a previously denied tool; it is unrelated to the missing allow entry.

Correct. MCP tools are exposed to Claude with the fully qualified name mcp__{server_name}__{tool_name}, so the allow rule must list mcp__weather__get_temperature, not just the bare function name, for it to auto-approve.
Bypassing permissions for the whole session is unnecessarily broad and approves every tool, not just this one; listing the specific tool in allowed_tools is the targeted fix.
The bare function name does not match the fully qualified tool name Claude actually calls, so an allow rule using just "get_temperature" would not match and would not auto-approve the call.
